bullets.title: IBM prelim Q2 miss triggers 20%+ crash; MSFT falls 2.8% in sympathy
bullets.body: IBM's preliminary Q2 results showed EPS of $2.27 vs. $3.02 estimate and revenue of $17.2B vs. $17.86B consensus, with infrastructure revenue down 7%. CEO cited unexpected capex reprioritization by clients in June and distraction from cybersecurity concerns — 'we did not anticipate the magnitude.' MSFT fell 2.8% premarket on spillover concern.

bullets.title: IBM CEO: clients shifted capex to servers/storage in late June, anticipating price hikes
bullets.body: IBM's CEO flagged that clients accelerated capex on servers, storage, and memory in late June ahead of anticipated price increases — a supply-driven demand pull-forward that hurt IBM's software/consulting pipeline. The capex reprioritization 'dynamic was not anticipated' in magnitude. Broader read-through for enterprise software demand is cautious.

bullets.title: SOXL rebalancing drove $6.5B+ forced semiconductor selling, amplifying semi correction
bullets.body: More than $6.5B of forced selling hit semiconductors during SOXL (3x leveraged semi ETF) rebalancing, amplifying the recent SOX correction. Tech monthly wrap commentary notes market has moved from 'unwind' to 'consolidation' phase with valuations reset and volatility stabilizing.

bullets.title: AI stocks forming bullish divergence; sellers exhausted — relief rally potential flagged
bullets.body: Fintwit technician notes AI stocks including DRAM names are 'trying to find a low for at least a relief rally,' citing bullish divergence and exhausted sellers. Risk of further downside acknowledged, but a multi-week recovery is viewed as plausible.

bullets.title: KeyBanc downgrades AAPL to Underweight with $250 PT; raises ARM target to $430
bullets.body: KeyBanc cut Apple to Underweight from Sector Perform with a $250 price target, signaling stock is at or near a peak. Separately, KeyBanc raised ARM Holdings' price target from $300 to $430, a 43% increase.

bullets.title: Bullish AAPL thesis: new hardware-focused CEO + M6/M7 chip ramp with significant RAM
bullets.body: One fintwit account expresses desire to buy more Apple on dips, citing the new CEO's hardware background and anticipated M6/M7 chips with major RAM increases. Stock viewed as currently fully valued but worth accumulating on weakness.

bullets.title: NVDA: NPO adoption could be next major growth leg post-2027 — 38M optical engine TAM by 2028
bullets.body: Analysis highlights NPO (network processing offload) adoption as a significant growth catalyst beyond 2027 as DSP removal increases analog content. NVIDIA and leading CSPs are actively evaluating NPO deployments, with the market forecast at 38M optical engines in 2028.

bullets.title: Google TPU 'ground war' escalates against NVIDIA's most loyal AI customers
bullets.body: Google is aggressively deploying TPU chips to compete directly with NVIDIA in AI accelerator market, targeting established NVIDIA customers. Separately, GOOGL signed one of the largest US clean energy deals: 2.5GW solar + 2.9GWh storage.

bullets.title: Tower Semiconductor jumps 18.6% premarket on ~$3B Japan government investment
bullets.body: TSEM surged 18.6% premarket after announcing approximately $3B in funding from the Japanese government to support chip manufacturing expansion. One trader flagged a long position in Jan 2028 $410 calls.

bullets.title: Nebius secures $1B+ AI compute deal with Reflection AI through 2029
bullets.body: Nebius (NBIS) agreed to sell more than $1 billion in AI computing capacity to Reflection AI in a contract extending through 2029, signaling continued hyperscale demand for AI infrastructure.

bullets.title: New York becomes first US state to enact one-year data center construction moratorium
bullets.body: Effective July 14, New York imposed a one-year moratorium on construction of large new data centers, the first such state-level action in the US. Implications for hyperscaler capacity expansion in the Northeast are under watch.

bullets.title: Market-implied July 29 FOMC rate hike odds climb to 45%; Fedspeak at most hawkish since Nov 2023
bullets.body: Markets are now pricing a 45% probability of a rate hike at the July 29 FOMC meeting. A Fedspeak sentiment model shows Chair Warsh at his most hawkish positioning since November 2023 ahead of congressional testimony.

bullets.title: CPI Tuesday: headline expected at 3.8%, core at 2.8% — Cleveland Fed nowcasts signal rolling over
bullets.body: Consensus expects June headline CPI to fall from 4.2% to 3.8% and core to edge down from 2.9% to 2.8%. Cleveland Fed nowcasts confirm headline rolling over from peak while core remains relatively firm.

bullets.title: Brent crude surges 5% to $87.49 on Iran blockade, US strikes, and Hormuz toll risk
bullets.body: Brent crude rallied 5% to $87.49/bbl — highest since June 12 — as the Iranian blockade began at 4 PM ET, US struck Abadan and Imam Khomeini Port, and Trump is reported 'very serious' about a 20% Hormuz transit fee. UK gilt yields broke above 5% on the energy spike. Bond volatility (MOVE) also surged.

bullets.title: NFIB Small Business Optimism surges to 97.4 in June — first uptick in outlook expectations this year
bullets.body: June NFIB Small Business Optimism rose to 97.4 vs. 95.7 consensus and 95.3 prior, the highest since February. Share of owners expecting better business conditions jumped to 10% from 3% — the first increase in forward outlook this year.

bullets.title: Goldman Sachs Q2 blowout: equities trading $7.42B vs. $5.02B est.; JPM equities $6.03B vs. $3.98B est.
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs Q2 revenue hit $20.34B with EPS of $20.98; equities sales & trading of $7.42B massively beat the $5.02B estimate. JPMorgan also beat with EPS $7.70 vs. $5.58 consensus, driven by equities trading of $6.03B vs. $3.98B est. and investment banking of $3.90B vs. $3.06B est.

bullets.title: SK Hynix cutting planned memory capacity additions to just 1/6 of original 2028 targets
bullets.body: SK Hynix is reportedly scaling back its memory capacity expansion to roughly one-sixth of planned additions by 2028, signaling significant capital discipline or a reassessment of demand trajectory in the memory market.

bullets.title: Consumer cyclical ETFs saw largest inflows week of 7/10; US large caps reversed to largest outflows
bullets.body: Flow data for the week ended July 10 showed consumer cyclical ETFs leading inflows while US large cap ETFs posted their largest outflows, reversing weeks of dominance — a notable rotation signal.

bullets.title: DeepSeek in early fundraising talks at ~$71B valuation
bullets.body: DeepSeek started preliminary talks this week with new investors on a funding round that would value the Chinese AI startup at approximately $71 billion pre-deal, per the FT. One observer believes the company is worth at least $150B.

bullets.title: AMZN becomes largest non-financial corporate issuer by market cap in JULI bond index
bullets.body: Amazon has surpassed all other non-financial issuers to become the largest by market value in the JULI corporate bond index, reflecting its dominant credit profile and scale.
